projects.overview: Studies incentives to acquire product-improvement information when downstream opportunities can be reallocated across routes. The project asks whether organizational reallocation changes the gap between privately optimal and system-optimal information acquisition.
projects.research_question: When can downstream reallocation reduce a firm's incentive to acquire information even though coordinated information acquisition becomes more valuable?
projects.mechanism: Reallocation changes which route captures the payoff from a discovery, shifting private appropriability relative to the system-wide value of information.

projects.overview: Studies entry when several peripheral platforms or hubs draw from a common residual market or network core. The application includes competition among regional co-creation hubs linked to a larger metropolitan or national core.
projects.research_question: How does entry by one peripheral option affect the profitability and welfare impact of entry by another when both interact through a shared core?
projects.mechanism: One entrant can thin the common core faced by others; network feedback on the core can amplify or reverse the resulting entry externality.

projects.overview: Studies standardization coalitions when firms can privately create compatibility after governments choose coalition structures. It examines whether private circumvention changes coalition incentives and stability.
projects.research_question: Can private compatibility overturn governments' preferred standardization coalition and the stability of exclusionary arrangements?
projects.mechanism: Private compatibility selectively erodes exclusion rents while leaving other market disadvantages intact, changing governments' payoff rankings.

projects.overview: A correction paper on the multi-firm implementation of undercut-proof pricing with downward-sloping demand. It revisits how switching-cost pricing should be computed when firms face non-flat demand.
projects.research_question: What pricing condition correctly characterizes undercut-proof prices in the multi-firm, downward-sloping-demand setting?
projects.mechanism: The correction restores the relevant demand response when evaluating whether a firm can profitably undercut its rivals.

projects.overview: A correction note on standardization unions and foreclosure. It studies pricing when an outsider may sell zero units but still constrain the prices chosen by coalition members.
projects.research_question: Can a foreclosed outsider remain strategically relevant even after its equilibrium sales fall to zero?
projects.mechanism: The outsider's potential re-entry through price competition creates a limit-pricing constraint before the market reaches an unconstrained duopoly regime.

projects.overview: A correction paper on R&D competition and cooperation with asymmetric spillovers. It re-examines the parameter boundaries used to compare individual and aggregate R&D outcomes.
projects.research_question: Are the published cutoff rules for comparing R&D outcomes valid throughout the admissible asymmetric-spillover parameter space?
projects.mechanism: Asymmetry makes the relevant comparison boundaries parameter-dependent, so fixed cutoffs can misclassify economically valid regions.

projects.overview: A correction candidate emerging from a replication audit of an oligopoly model with a residual-monopoly stage. The project tests whether the reported equilibrium profile is robust to unilateral deviations.
projects.research_question: Does the published residual-monopoly pricing profile satisfy the underlying best-response conditions throughout the stated parameter region?
projects.mechanism: A local pricing deviation can alter continuation payoffs and, if profitable, propagate to upstream capacity and welfare calculations.

projects.overview: Studies decentralized R&D choices by regional public research institutes that choose both research capacity and research direction. The application includes public laboratories and cultivar or technology development.
projects.research_question: When do decentralized regional laboratories choose too much duplication or too little diversification relative to the socially desirable research portfolio?
projects.mechanism: Discovery correlation, failure insurance, commercialization, and downstream product-market substitution jointly determine the value of parallel versus diversified research.
